study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Jalbrzikowski et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2019
study_identification_part.si4_title: Age-Associated Deviations of Amygdala Functional Connectivity in Youths With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: Relevance to Psychotic Symptoms

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the objectives: to create normative growth charts of amygdala functional connectivity in typically developing youths, assess age-associated deviations in youths with psychosis spectrum disorders, and examine relationships with positive symptoms. This specifies both the research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Objective: The authors created normative growth charts of amygdala functional connectivity in typically developing youths, assessed age-associated deviations of these trajectories in youths with psychosis spectrum disorders, and explored how these disruptions are related to clinical symptomatology.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Eligibility criteria for the typically developing (reference) cohorts are described for Luna 1/2 (no psychiatric disorders, IQ thresholds, no MRI contraindications). Image quality standards and data completeness are specified via motion QC (FD>0.3 mm and/or DVARS>20 censored; subjects dropped if >20% volumes removed). Final sample sizes are reported in the abstract and Table 1 (e.g., 622 typically developing).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: For Luna 1 and Luna 2, participants and their first-degree relatives did not have a psychiatric disorder... Exclusion criteria... IQ lower than 80... or any MRI contraindications. ... We censored and removed volumes that had an FD > 0.3 mm and/or DVARS > 20 ... Subjects were dropped from rsfMRI analyses if more than 20% of their volumes were removed. ... 1,062 participants 10–25 years of age (622 typically developing control youths...).

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The modeling includes age, sex, and site as fixed effects, subject as a random effect (to account for repeated measures), and additional analyses including average framewise displacement to address motion. Site effects are explicitly considered.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: We used the 3dLME program in AFNI... Subject was included as a random effect... Age, sex, and site were included as fixed effects. ... We... reran the linear mixed-effects models, including average framewise displacement as an additional fixed effect.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort is drawn from multiple specified samples (Luna 1, Luna 2, PNC, Pitt). The PNC dataset source and access pathway (dbGaP) are described. The study design for each cohort is listed in Table 1.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Data for the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort (PNC) was obtained through the Database of Genotypes and Phenotypes platform... The Pitt sample was recruited from an ongoing Conte Center study... TABLE 1. Demographic information for all samples... (Luna 1, Luna 2, Philadelphia, Pitt).

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Imaging modality (resting-state fMRI and structural MPRAGE) and equipment (Siemens 3T Tim Trio) are specified. Acquisition parameters (TR/TE, flip angle, voxel size, instructions, acquisition time) are provided per cohort in Table S2 of the supplement.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: For all samples, scanning data were acquired using Siemens 3-T Tim Trio scanners. Resting-state data were collected using an echo-planar sequence... A magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo sequence (MPRAGE) was acquired... Table S2... includes scan instructions and parameters. ... TR/TE (ms) ... Flip angle ... Voxel size ... Instructions ... Acquisition time.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps are detailed: removal of initial volumes, normalization to MNI space, spatial smoothing, wavelet despiking, nuisance regression (NBT/WM/CSF/motion and derivatives), bandpass filtering, ICA-AROMA, scrubbing with FD/DVARS thresholds, and subject exclusion if >20% volumes censored. Software used includes FreeSurfer, FSL (FNIRT), and AFNI.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: The first 4 TRs from all scans were removed... warped into MNI standard space ... smoothed using a 5-mm ... Wavelet Despiking ... simultaneous multiple regression of nuisance variables and bandpass filtering at 0.009 Hz < f < 0.08... nuisance regressors ... created using Freesurfer... ICA-Aroma was implemented... We censored and removed volumes that had an FD > 0.3 mm and/or DVARS > 20 ... Subjects were dropped ... if more than 20% of their volumes were removed.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study models normative trajectories using all typically developing data with linear mixed-effects analyses. There is no description of a hold-out set, K-fold cross-validation, or any partitioning strategy where the model is tested on unseen samples for internal validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: We used the 3dLME program in AFNI to examine voxelwise developmental effects of age for each amygdala subregion in typically developing control youths... Age, sex, and site were included as fixed effects.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No application of the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset (not used for model development) is described.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No statement of external validation beyond the multi-cohort development sample; analyses focus on group-by-age interactions and deviation scores within the combined dataset.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.location: Jalbrzikowski2019.pdf.md (methods/results sections); no explicit external validation reported

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: Normative trajectories are estimated with voxelwise linear mixed-effects models (AFNI 3dLME), testing linear, inverse, and quadratic age functions, with subject as random effect and fixed effects for age/sex/site. First-level seed-based connectivity is computed using AFNI 3dDeconvolve and 3dREMLfit.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: We conducted voxelwise regressions ... using AFNI's 3dDeconvolve... AFNI's 3dREMLfit... We used the 3dLME program in AFNI... Subject was included as a random effect... Age, sex, and site were included as fixed effects. Linear, inverse, and quadratic forms of age were examined.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The study reports statistical significance of developmental effects and cluster-level corrections but does not provide quantitative model fit metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, calibration, or coverage of prediction intervals) for the normative model.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Results were corrected for multiple comparisons using a combination of cluster size and voxel probability... (no metrics such as R^2 or prediction error reported).

Image quality standards and exclusion thresholds are specified. Final clinical sample sizes are provided (e.g., 194 psychosis spectrum; 246 other psychopathology).

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses consider clinical symptom severity beyond demographics by relating deviation scores to positive symptoms in the psychosis spectrum group; positive and negative symptom measures are explicitly defined from SIPS/PS-R items.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Positive and negative symptoms were measured by summing the relevant Structured Interview for Prodromal Syndromes/PRIME Screen-Revised responses...
